title: Typing map/filter/reduce callbacks precisely
hook: Array.map, filter, and reduce infer callback parameter types from the array element type — but generic pipelines, tuple returns, and reduce accumulators need explicit type parameters or overloads to stay precise.

blocks.text: TypeScript types **Array.prototype** methods using generic signatures. `arr.map(cb)` infers `cb`'s parameter from `arr`'s element type `T` and return from `cb`'s return type `U`, producing `U[]`. **filter** with a type predicate `(x): x is U` narrows to `U[]`. **reduce** is the trickiest — accumulator type defaults from optional initial value or requires explicit generic `reduce<U>(...)`. **flatMap** chains map and flatten with typed depth. Mis-typed reduce is a top source of `any` leakage in codebases.

entries.plainDefinition: Transforms T[] to U[] based on callback return type.
filter((x): x is U => ...) narrows array to U[].
Second type param U in reduce<U> — accumulator and return type.
map then flatten one level — return U | U[] from callback.

blocks.text: Data pipelines in ETL, React selectors, and API aggregation chains use map/filter/reduce daily. Untyped reduce often widens to `any` when initial value is omitted. filter without type predicate returns `T[]` even when you removed non-matching types at runtime. C# LINQ's `Select`, `Where`, `Aggregate` are method-based with explicit generics; TypeScript relies on inference with escape hatches. Senior interviews ask how to type `groupBy`, `partition`, and custom `reduce` without `any`.

blocks.title: filter narrowing
blocks.body: Use type predicate in filter to get Admin[] from User[] — plain filter(Boolean) does not narrow.

diagram.title: Typed array pipeline
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  A[T[]] -->|map| B[U[]]
  B -->|filter is U| C[U[]]
  C -->|reduce U,R| D[R]

snippet.label: filter with type predicate
snippet.explanation: Line 9: type predicate tells compiler survivors are Admin. Without `u is Admin`, result stays User[].

snippet.label: reduce with explicit accumulator
snippet.explanation: Line 4: reduce<number> with initial 0 — accumulator typed. Line 8: object accumulator needs explicit Record generic — empty {} alone infers poorly.

snippet.label: flatMap for split-and-flatten
snippet.explanation: flatMap callback returns U | readonly U[] — split returns string[] flattened one level. Conditional return types union array and empty.

snippet.label: Failure mode — reduce without initial on empty array
snippet.explanation: reduce without initial uses first element as accumulator — empty array throws at runtime. Always guard length or provide initial value.

blocks.title: filter(Boolean) does not narrow
blocks.body: Use type predicate or dedicated isDefined helper with `x is NonNullable<T>`.

blocks.title: reduce to any via {} initial
blocks.body: Empty object accumulator without Record<string, T> generic widens to any in strict mode.

blocks.text: Build typed `groupBy<T, K extends string>(items: T[], key: (t: T) => K): Record<K, T[]>` with generics. `Array.from` with mapFn types iterables. Readonly arrays use same methods but return readonly results in TS 5.0+. For performance-sensitive code, for-loops beat map for V8 optimization — types work identically. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` affects reduce/index access inside callbacks.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Easy to forget on object acc

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot type reduce accumulator. Thinking filter narrows without predicate. reduce on empty array without initial.

interviewTakeaways: map infers U[] from callback return; filter needs type predicate to narrow.
reduce<U>(fn, init) — always provide initial for object accumulators and empty arrays.
flatMap = map + flatten one level; callback returns U | U[].
60s: Type predicates in filter for Admin[]. Explicit reduce generic for Record accumulators. Guard empty reduce. any in chain poisons inference.
Follow-up: groupBy generic, ReadonlyArray map return types.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "map/filter types are automatic" — reduce and filter narrowing need care.
filter(x => x.role === 'admin') without predicate — still User[].
Strong: "Type predicate in filter. reduce<U> with initial. Never reduce empty without init."

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS map/filter/reduce are untyped — TS adds inference and type predicates for compile-time pipeline safety.
C# LINQ Where/Select use explicit generics; TS relies on callback inference with type predicates as the narrowing bridge.
